sentences.text:
(Manoj Rathour Vs The State Of Madhya Prades
 Dated : 08-11-2024
Shri Dependra Mishra - Advocate for appellant.

Ms. Nupur Dhamija - Deputy Government 
 respondent/State.
Shri Amit Dwivedi - Advocate for objector.

Heard on I.A. No.17884 of 2024 which is a a repeat application for suspension of sentence on behalf of the appellant - Manoj Rathour who has been convicted under Sections 366, 342, 376(2) (n) and 506-II of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 5 years and to pay fine of Rs.1000/-; R.I. for 1 year and to pay fine of Rs.1000/-; R.I. for 20 years and to pay fine of Rs.1000/-; and R.I. for 5 years and to pay fine of Rs.1000/- respectively, with default stipulations as mentioned in the impugned judgment dated 25.05.2023 passed by the learned Second Additional Sessions Judge, Anuppur in S.T. No.80 of 2019.
His first application was dismissed on merits vide order dated 07.08.2023.

This application has been filed on the ground of parity with other co- accused Raju Rathore who has been enlarged on bail by the Hon'ble Supreme Court vide order dated 12.06.2024 passed in Criminal Appeal No.2767 of 2024.
considering the ground that victim is lawfully wedded with appellant Manoj Rathour against whom allegation of rape was there.
The victim is having two children and now residing happily with the family members of 2 CRA-7684-2023 the present appellant, therefore, the co-accused has been enlarged on bail.
The appellant is having no criminal case registered against him.
The appeal would take long time for its final conclusion.

Hence,
sentence of appellant be suspended during pendency of appeal.

Learned counsel appearing for the objector has no objection for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant contending therein that the victim has already solemnized marriage with appellant Manoj Rathour and she is having two children and she does not want to object the application.

sentences.text: Learned counsel appearing for the State could not dispute the fact that co-accused Raju Rathour has already been enlarged on bail by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.

Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the matter, this Court deems it appropriate to allow the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

Accordingly, I.A. No.17884 of 2024 is allowed and it is directed that the remaining jail sentence of the appellant shall remain under suspension subject to the verification that the amount of fine has been deposited and the appellant is the first offender.

It is directed that he be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the trial Court/concerned Court on 15.01.2024 and thereafter on such other 3 CRA-7684-2023 subsequent dates as may be fixed in that behalf.
List the appeal for final hearing in due course.
I.A.No.24914 of 2024 stands disposed off.
(VISHAL MISHRA) (AVANINDRA KU  JUDGE JUDG
